description: Applies §8.1's version acceptance and refusal rules: a tool interprets a document only when the document's `major.minor` line is one the tool supports, and produces a version refusal otherwise, in either direction. The patch number carries no meaning, so a tool that supports a line accepts every patch of it, including patches published after the tool. Build metadata is ignored; a prerelease is not part of its line and is accepted only when the tool declares support for that specific prerelease. Supporting one line implies nothing about another.
notes: Tests assume the SDK under test supports a set of lines bounded below `999.x` for major-version refusal cases, and bounded below `0.999.x` for pre-1.0 minor-version refusal cases. SDK conformance to OBI-T-04 is independent of which lines the SDK supports; the refusal tests assert behavior on documents declaring versions outside any plausible SDK's supported lines in this version family. Downward refusal (a document declaring a line below the SDK's supported lines MUST be refused rather than processed under the wrong rules) is fixtured with `requiresMinSupported`: those tests apply only to SDKs whose lowest supported version is at or above the annotation's value, and are skipped (reported separately) for SDKs whose lines extend down to the document's version. Acceptance-presuming positives are gated with `requiresSupports` (the acceptance-gate annotation; see the corpus README): each is administered only to tools that support the annotation version's line, since which lines a tool supports is its own declaration. Every positive here carries `requiresSupports: "0.2.0"`, so for a tool that supports the 0.2 line the higher-patch cases assert §8.1's rule that the patch number does not enter the decision. The prerelease case stays ungated: a prerelease MUST NOT be accepted unless the tool declares support for that specific prerelease (`0.2.0-rc.1` asserts default rejection by a tool that has not opted in; the opt-in exception is not separately fixtured).

tests.description: document declares the current spec version (administered only to tools that support the 0.2 line)
build metadata is ignored in comparison; `0.2.0+build.1` is treated as `0.2.0` (administered only to tools that support the 0.2 line)
a tool that supports the 0.2 line accepts a higher patch within it: the patch number carries no meaning (administered only to tools that support the 0.2 line)
a tool that supports the 0.2 line accepts a patch published after the tool: the document is read under the line (administered only to tools that support the 0.2 line)
a prerelease is not accepted unless the tool declares support for that specific prerelease (default rejection)
document declares a major version higher than any plausible SDK supports
document declares a far-future major version with non-zero minor
pre-1.0 document declares a higher minor than any plausible SDK's supported set
pre-1.0 document declares a higher minor with a patch component
downward refusal: pre-1.0 document declares a lower minor outside the SDK's supported set (refused rather than processed under the wrong rules)
downward refusal: a higher patch on an unsupported lower minor is still outside the set (patch never rescues a refused minor)
